answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake and earn a slow, non-transferable reputation score before transacting at scale. Like a falcon returning to the same knoll, a genuine agent builds verifiable history over time, while a marble token deposit makes spawning thousands of fake identities expensive: an attacker must fund every clone and wait through the same probationary work, so cost grows linearly with each fake while an honest agent pays once.
